MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING
  OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  LA VERNE

  Monday, March 15, 2021

1.  In order to minimize the spread of the COVID- 19 Virus, Governor Newsom issued an Executive Order that
  temporarily suspends  requirements  of the  Brown Act.  The Council Chambers was closed to the public, La Verne
  City Council Members and members of the public attended this meeting telephonically, and meeting was live
  streamed on the City' s website.

2.  A regular meeting of the La Verne City Council was called to order by Mayor Hepburn at 6: 30 p. m.

3.  Council Members  present:  Mayor Tim Hepburn
  Mayor Pro Tem Robin Carder
  Council Member Muir Davis
  Council Member Wendy Lau
  Council Member Rick Crosby

  Absent:  None.

  Advisory personnel  present:  City Manager Robert Russi
  Assistant to the City Manager JR Ranells
  City Attorney Robert L. Kress
  Assistant City Clerk Lupe Gaeta Estrella
  Interim Finance Director Mark Alvarado
  Senior Management Analyst Christy Lopez

4.  Pledge of Allegiance was led by Council Member Davis.

5.  Announcements  of  Upcoming  Mayor Hepburn called for any public announcements and waited for staff to
  Community Events  check for any announcements via telephone communication.

  There was none.

6.  Consent Calendar  It was moved by Davis seconded by Carder, and unanimously carried by roll
  call to accept, approve, or act on the Consent Calendar items.

  City Council Minutes of March  1, 2021,  were received and filed.

  The agreement between the City of La Verne and County of Los Angeles
  Agricultural Commissioner/Weights and Measures Department for Weed
  Abatement services expires on June 30, 2021. The County of Los Angeles
  requested approval of a renewal agreement now to allow sufficient time for
  approval by the Board of Supervisors prior to expiration of the current
  agreement.

  City Manager Russi recommended that the City Council adopt Resolution No.
  21- 13, approving an agreement with the County of Los Angeles for continued
  weed abatement services for the period of July 1, 2021 through June 30, 2026.
  Approved.

Resolution  No. 21- 14,  Resolution  No. 21- 14 -  A RESOLUTION  OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE

California Climate Investment  APPROVING THE APPLICATION FOR GRANT FUNDS FOR CALIFORNIA
Urban  Greening Program  CLIMATE INVESTMENTS URBAN GREENING PROGRAM.

  The City Council approved Resolution No. 21- 10, at its February 15, 2021,
  meeting approving the City' s submission of a grant application for the Urban
  Greening Program. Unfortunately, the grant administrator with the California
  Natural Resources Administration did not accept the resolution as it did not
  meet the state' s required format. Staff, therefore, submitted a revised
  resolution for Council approval.

  Interim Public Works Director Keesey recommended that the City Council
  approve Resolution No. 21- 14, authorizing the submission of an Urban
  Greening Grant application to the California Natural Resources Administration
  and further designating the Director of Public Works as the person authorized
  to act on the City' s behalf with respect to the grant application.

White Paper  on  LAHSA  Reform  OF GOVERNMENTS'  WHITE  PAPER  ON LAHSA  REFORM. Approved.
   Page 3
  City Council Minutes, Monday, March 15, 2021,

  The San Gabriel Valley Council  of  Governments ( SGVCOG), in collaboration
  with its member cities, has developed and adopted a white paper addressing
  the shortcomings of the current homelessness  services system within Los
  Angeles County, and providing recommendations for reforms, specifically in
  relation to the operations of the Los Angeles Homeless Services Authority
  LAHSA), to improve the delivery of services to reduce homelessness. To
  demonstrate the City' s support for the implementation of the proposed
  recommendations identified within the white paper, staff has prepared
  Resolution No. 21- 15 for the City Council' s consideration.

  Community Development Director Scherer recommended that the City Council
  approve Resolution No. 21- 15 authorizing the adoption of the SGVCOG White
  Paper on LAHSA Reform ( Attachment A). Approved.

  Mayor Hepburn called for public comment on this matter.

  Following the protest hearing, it was moved by Crosby, seconded by Lau, and

  Commissioner/ Director of Weights &  Measures to abate the nuisance by
  having weeds, rubbish, and refuse removed for the two subject properties.

8.  Mid- Year Financial Report  Interim Finance Director Alvarado reported on the Mid- Year Financial Report.
  He stated that the 2020- 21 Budget was approved by the City Council on June
  30, 2020.  Based on economic changes that have occurred since then, the
  Finance Division is now providing a mid- year financial update report for the
  2020- 21 fiscal year.

  Interim Finance Director Alvarado stated that assumptions were incorporated
  into the budget based on the 2019- 20 fourth quarter economic ramifications of
  COVID- 19 known at that time. As part of the budget adoption, City staff
  planned to come back to the City Council with updates at approximately three-
  month intervals. The report to Council formally acknowledges those updates,
  as well as addressing additional changes that have occurred.

  Interim Finance Director Alvarado reported on sales tax revenue, property
  taxes, motor vehicle- in- lieu fee, Fire Department' s Ambulance Transport
  Services, and Fire Assignment Program, General Fund Expenditures, Measure
  LV Sales Tax and  on  the Mid- Year Budget amendments.
   City Council Minutes, Monday, March 15, 2021,  Page 4

  It was moved by Davis and seconded by Carder and unanimously carried by
  roll call to approve the budget amendments detailed in the included Budget
  Amendments  Listing ( attached to the staff report), to adjust revenues and
  expenditure appropriations for the fiscal year 2020- 21 budget. These
  adjustments will better align our budgets with expected results for the current
  fiscal year.

  Council Member Davis commended the Finance Department and that he was
  appreciative  of all their hard work.

9.  COVID- 19 Update  City Manager Russi reported that Los Angeles County, as of today, has met
  the State' s threshold to reopen key sectors in the community and will permit a
  wide range of indoor operations to resume in sectors including; middle and
  high schools; restaurants; movie theaters; gyms; museums, zoos and
  aquariums, all with safeguards in place.

  City Manager Russi reported that due to Waste Management staffing changes
  due to COVID- 19 recycling pick- ups will be delayed for certain parts of the
  City.

10.  Public Comment  This was the time set aside for anyone wishing to address the City Council on
  items not listed in any other  place  on  the agenda.  Mayor Hepburn called for
  public comment and waited for staff to check for any public comment via
  telephone  communication.

  Mayor Hepburn  called  for public  comment.  The following individual was called.

  Robert Russell

  To hear what was said during public comment, please visit the City' s website
  to view the archived Council meeting.

  Two public comments received via email ( attached).

  She stated  she  is thrilled  with  the reopening  of sectors  of  the City.  She urged

  everyone to continue wearing their mask and thanked the Community for their
  support in this effort. She also gave an update on the Gold Line Construction
  and stated the time frame for completion has changed.

  Council Member Davis joined Mayor Pro Tem Carder in thanking City Manager
  Russi for his COVD- 19 update. He urged those who are eligible to get
  vaccinated  and he said that eventually everyone would be eligible. He stated
